summary: There are four main kinds of damage: an ox, a pit, an animal eating (or a person), and fire. Each one is different, but the owner must always guard them, and if they do damage he must pay from his best land.

chunks.en: There are four main kinds of damage:
chunks.st: There are four primary categories of damage:

words.note: Avos means "fathers": the main groups that other kinds of damage come from.

chunks.en: The ox, the pit, the maveh, and the fire.
chunks.explain: Maveh is an animal eating with its teeth, or a person.
chunks.st: The category of Ox; and the category of Pit; and the category of Maveh,
chunks.stMore: which, based on a discussion in the Gemara refers either to the tooth of an animal that causes damage or to a person who causes damage; and the category of Fire. Each of these categories is unique; therefore, the halakhot of one cannot be derived from another.

words.note: A hole someone dug and left open.
The Gemara says this is an animal's tooth, or a person.

chunks.en: The ox is not like the maveh,
chunks.st: The defining characteristic of the primary category of Ox is not similar to the defining characteristic of the primary category of Maveh,

chunks.en: and the maveh is not like the ox.
chunks.st: and the defining characteristic of the primary category of Maveh is not similar to the defining characteristic of the primary category of Ox.

chunks.en: And these two,
chunks.st: And the defining characteristics of this category of Ox and that category of Maveh,

chunks.en: which are alive,
chunks.st: in which there is a living spirit that causes damage,

chunks.en: are not like fire,
chunks.st: are not similar to the defining characteristic of the category of Fire,

chunks.en: which is not alive.
chunks.st: in which there is no living spirit.

chunks.en: And these,
chunks.st: The mishna continues: And the defining characteristics of this primary category of Ox and Maveh and that primary category of Fire,

chunks.en: which usually move around and do damage,
chunks.st: in which the typical manner of their components is to proceed from one place to another and cause damage,

chunks.en: are not like a pit,
chunks.st: are not similar to the defining characteristic of the primary category of Pit,

chunks.en: which does not move around to do damage.
chunks.explain: The pit stays still; someone walks into it.
chunks.st: in which the typical manner of its components is not to proceed from one place to another and cause damage;
chunks.stMore: rather, it remains in place and the damage is caused by the injured party proceeding and encountering the obstacle.

chunks.en: What they all have in common
chunks.st: The common denominator of the components in all of these primary categories is

chunks.en: is that they usually do damage, and you must guard them.
chunks.st: that it is their typical manner to cause damage, and the responsibility for their safeguarding to prevent them from causing damage is incumbent upon you,
chunks.stMore: the owner of the animal or generator of the fire or the pit.

chunks.en: And when one does damage, the one who caused it must pay for the damage
chunks.st: And when a component of any of these categories causes damage, the owner or generator of the component that caused the damage is obligated to pay restitution

chunks.en: from the best of his land.
chunks.st: for damage with best-quality land.

summary: If I am supposed to guard something and it does damage, it is as if I did the damage myself. The mishnah also lists which property and which places a person must pay for.

chunks.en: Anything I must guard,
chunks.st: With regard to anything for which I became responsible for safeguarding it to prevent it from causing damage,

chunks.en: I am the one who made its damage happen.
chunks.st: if it in fact causes damage, it is considered as if I actively facilitated that damage, and accordingly I must pay for it.

chunks.en: If I made part of its damage happen,
chunks.st: In any case in which I facilitated part of the damage it caused,

chunks.en: I must pay as if I made all of its damage happen.
chunks.st: I am liable for payments of restitution for damage it caused, as if I were the one who facilitated the entire damage it caused.

chunks.en: One pays only for things that are not hekdesh,
chunks.explain: Hekdesh is property that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: One is liable only with regard to damage caused to property for which, were he to use it for a non-sacred purpose, he would not be liable for the misuse of consecrated property;

words.note: Using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: for things that belong to Jews,
chunks.st: with regard to damage caused to property that belongs to members of the covenant, i.e., Jews;

words.note: Jews, who are part of Hashem's bris.

chunks.en: for things that belong to a certain owner,
chunks.st: and with regard to assigned property,
chunks.stMore: the meaning of which the Gemara will explain.

chunks.en: and in any place except a place that belongs only
chunks.st: And one is liable for damage caused in any place except for a domain designated exclusively

chunks.en: to the one who did the damage, and in a place shared by both of them.
chunks.st: for the use of the one responsible for the damage. And one is liable for damage caused in a domain designated for the joint use of the injured party and the one liable for the damage.

chunks.en: And when one does damage, the one who caused it must pay for the damage
chunks.st: When an animal or item one is responsible to safeguard causes damage, the one liable for the damage caused by insufficiently safeguarding it is obligated to pay payments of restitution

chunks.en: from the best of his land.
chunks.st: for damage with his best-quality land.

summary: This mishnah gives rules about how damages are judged: the value is set in money, by a beis din, with proper witnesses. Women are included, and both sides take part in the payment.

chunks.en: The damage is judged in money,
chunks.st: The determination of payment of damages is made by monetary appraisal.

chunks.en: one pays with things worth money,
chunks.st: One pays with items worth money.

chunks.en: in front of a beis din,
chunks.st: This halakha applies before a court.

words.note: A beis din is a Jewish court.

chunks.en: by the word of witnesses who are
chunks.st: And it is based upon the testimony of witnesses who are

chunks.en: free men and Jews.
chunks.st: free men, i.e., men who are not Canaanite slaves, and who are members of the covenant, i.e., Jews.

chunks.en: And women are included in the laws of damages.
chunks.st: And women are included in the halakhot of damages in the same way as men.

chunks.en: And the one who was hurt and the one who did damage are both part of the payment.
chunks.st: And both the injured party and the one liable for the damage are involved in the payment.
chunks.stMore: The Gemara will explicate each of these principles.

words.en: and the one who was damaged

summary: Some animals are "tam" (not known to do harm), and the owner pays half. Some are "mu'ad" (known to do harm), and the owner pays in full. The mishnah lists which is which.

chunks.en: There are five that are tam, and five that are mu'ad.
chunks.explain: Tam: not known to harm. Mu'ad: known to harm, so pays fully.
chunks.st: There are five damage-causing acts that an animal can perform twice and remain innocuous even when its owner was warned each time to prevent it from doing so.
chunks.stMore: After the third time, the animal is rendered forewarned. In such cases, the owner is liable to pay only half of the damages. And there are five damage-causing acts for which an animal is considered forewarned, at times even if it had never caused damage in that manner. In such cases the owner is liable to pay the full cost of the damage.

words.note: An animal not known to do this harm; the owner pays half.
Warned, known to do this harm; the owner pays in full.

chunks.en: An animal is not mu'ad to gore,
chunks.st: An animal is not considered forewarned with regard to Goring, i.e., not for goring with its horns,

chunks.en: or to push, or to bite, or
chunks.st: nor for pushing with its body, nor for biting,

chunks.en: to lie down on things, or to kick.
chunks.st: nor for crouching upon items in order to damage them, nor for kicking.
chunks.stMore: In these cases the animal is considered to be innocuous and its owner is liable for only half of the damages.

chunks.he: הַשֵּׁן מוּעֶדֶת לֶאֱכֹל אֶת הָרָאוּי לָהּ,
chunks.en: The tooth is mu'ad to eat what it usually eats.
chunks.st: Concerning acts of damage performed with the tooth, the animal is considered forewarned with regard to eating that which is fitting for it to eat.

chunks.en: The foot is mu'ad to break things while walking.
chunks.st: Concerning acts of damage performed with the foot, the animal is considered forewarned with regard to breaking items while walking.

chunks.en: And an ox that is mu'ad,
chunks.explain: An ox that gored three times, and its owner was warned.
chunks.st: And there is a forewarned ox, which gored three times and each time his owner was warned to safeguard his ox from doing so.

chunks.en: and an ox that does damage on the land of the one it hurt,
chunks.st: And there is an ox that causes damage to the property of the injured party while on the property of the injured party.

chunks.he: וְהָאָדָם. הַזְּאֵב וְהָאֲרִי וְהַדֹּב וְהַנָּמֵר וְהַבַּרְדְּלָס וְהַנָּחָשׁ,
chunks.en: and a person. The wolf, the lion, the bear, the leopard, the bardelas, and the snake:
chunks.st: And there is the person, i.e., any damage done by a person.
chunks.stMore: In all of these cases the one who caused the damage is considered to be forewarned, resulting in the obligation to pay the full cost of the damage. The mishna presents the halakha for wild animals: The wolf; the lion; the bear; the leopard; the bardelas, the meaning of which the Gemara will discuss; and the snake.

words.note: A wild animal; the Gemara discusses which one.

chunks.en: these are mu'ad.
chunks.st: These are considered forewarned even if they had never previously caused damage.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: When they are tame,
chunks.st: When these animals are domesticated

chunks.en: they are not mu'ad.
chunks.st: they are not considered forewarned.

chunks.en: But the snake is always mu'ad.
chunks.st: But the snake is always considered forewarned.

chunks.en: What is the difference between tam and mu'ad?
chunks.st: What is the difference between the liability incurred for damage caused by an ox that is considered innocuous and the liability incurred for damage caused by an ox that is forewarned?

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁהַתָּם מְשַׁלֵּם חֲצִי נֶזֶק מִגּוּפוֹ,
chunks.en: Only that a tam pays half the damage, from its own body,
chunks.explain: The owner pays only from selling the ox itself.
chunks.st: The only differences are that for damage caused by an innocuous ox, the owner pays half the cost of the damage exclusively from proceeds of the sale of the body of the ox,

chunks.he: וּמוּעָד מְשַׁלֵּם נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם מִן הָעֲלִיָּה:
chunks.en: and a mu'ad pays the full damage from the best property.
chunks.st: and for a forewarned ox he pays the full cost of the damage from his higher property.
